summary: One of the problems, every farmer face is the pests and deaseas. When trying to manage huge fields, farmers often rely on their intuitive senses or repeat what their families did when it comes to planting plants. But do they know that all the pests and deaseas can be dealed with through scientifically proven schemas. Our website does exactly that. We pull NASA data and our machine analyzes everything and gives best orders to create most profit, to save most water, to protect from pests or all at once.
details:
1. Data Ingestion & Verification Layer (Zero-Key Architecture)

​When a user enters a town, valley, or GPS coordinate (e.g., 41.2995° N, 69.2401° E), the frontend directly queries five public Earth science and weather endpoints without requiring user API keys, logging every raw granule ID and sync timestamp for full auditability:

​Soil Moisture (NASA SMAP L4 via NSIDC / CMR & POWER): Measures both surface topsoil moisture (0–5 cm) and deeper root-zone water reserves (%).

​Canopy Health (NASA HLS 10–30m via LPCLOUD Earthdata STAC / CMR): Fuses Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery to calculate high-resolution vegetation greenness indices (NDVI and EVI) for the specific plot.

​Precipitation & Water Deficit (NASA GPM & IMERG via GES DISC & POWER): Tracks actual rainfall (mm) and compares it against crop evapotranspiration/water demand to compute irrigation gaps.

​Agroclimatology & Thermal Baseline (NASA POWER & MODIS/TS): Pulls 16-day rolling daily granules alongside historical seasonal curves for daytime max air temperature, nighttime minimums, and ground skin temperature (°C).

​14-Day Weather & Frost Forecast (Open-Meteo API): Provides near-term rainfall totals and minimum temperature alerts (e.g., detecting overnight drops to 1.4°C–1.9°C). ​Soil Baseline (ISRIC SoilGrids / Regional Fallback): Resolves local soil texture (e.g., Silty Clay Loam), pH (7.4), and organic humus (2.1%) at the target coordinates to establish water-retention and nutrient baselines.

​2. Core Analytical Engines

​A. Crop Survival Predictor & Risk Matrix

​The system cross-references live telemetry and 14-day forecasts against crop-specific physiological thresholds (e.g., Tomatoes requiring 18°C–29°C and pH 6.0–6.8) to score real-time survival odds across four vectors: ​Cold / Frost Risk: Triggers high-risk alerts when forecast lows breach crop tolerance (e.g., nights dropping to 1.4°C–1.9°C drop survival odds to 20%–46% and recommend row covers or delaying planting).

​Soil Water Risk: Compares SMAP root-zone moisture (e.g., 17% vs. 37%) against upcoming Open-Meteo rainfall to flag drought stress before wilting occurs. ​Heat Stress Risk: Monitors daytime highs and MODIS land skin temperature, triggering shade-cloth advisories above 34°C when tomato pollen viability drops. ​Soil Disease Risk: Evaluates crop-family rotation history to estimate soil-borne blight and rot pressure.

​B. 4-Season Rotation Generator & Live Auditor

​Using the location's climate zone, soil pH, and humus profile, the rotation engine works in two modes: ​Goal-Driven Synthesis: Builds an optimized 4-season sequence around an anchor cash crop (selected by user) one of three priorities: Save Water & Beat Drought, Feed the Soil Naturally, or Stop Plant Diseases & Pests. It pairs high-value crops with winter soil blankets, nitrogen-fixing legumes, and deep-rooted soil breakers, calculating water savings per season and overall climate fit.

​Interactive Custom Audit: Lets farmers test their own 4-season crop sequences and immediately runs a validation check—scoring overall survival odds (e.g., 92%), water reduction (38%), botanical family repetition (flagging back-to-back disease risks), nitrogen recharge, and seasonal temperature compatibility.

​3. Agronomy Translation & User Workflows ​TARS AI Farm Advisor & "Ask TARS" Co-Pilot: Synthesizes raw numbers into plain-language daily guidance—calculating exact watering intervals based on current root-zone moisture, issuing weekly field tasks (such as applying 5–7 cm of straw mulch to cut evaporation and block soil-splash blight), and providing harvest/post-harvest storage rules.

​Analytics & Telemetry Transparency: Visualizes annual seasonal curves alongside a 16-day raw NASA POWER observation table and one-click Inspect Raw JSON links so agronomists or farmers can verify every single reading directly against NASA servers. ​Offline Portability: Exports the complete plot state, satellite readings, and customized rotation plan into a standalone .json farm report
